summary: Learn R programming for data science with our comprehensive training. Master data analysis and visualization techniques to advance your career.
lede: Data science with R training helps analysts, researchers, and managers build repeatable workflows for turning datasets into analysis and reports. You’ll practice cleaning and transforming data with dplyr, exploring and visualizing it with ggplot2, producing reproducible reports in R Markdown, and applying basic statistics and regression modeling.
audienceIntro: You should join this course if you work with data and need to move beyond manual tools into reliable R programming for data science. The training is tailored for analysts, researchers, and managers who want to build practical, repeatable R workflows that support serious analytics and reporting in their teams. This course is designed for: Data Analyst using spreadsheets who must transition analyses into R scripts. Business Intelligence Analyst responsible for building R-based visualizations and reports. Junior Data Scientist implementing data wrangling and models in R workflows. Research Analyst performing statistical analysis and reproducible reporting with R. Marketing Analytics Specialist exploring campaign data using dplyr and ggplot2. Operations Data Specialist automating KPI calculations and dashboards in R. Financial Analytics Professional validating models and stress tests using R code. Healthcare Data Scientist managing clinical datasets with R and tidyverse. Risk Analytics Associate building R Markdown reports for leadership oversight. Analytics Manager overseeing R-based data science projects and code quality.
modules: Control Flow, Functions, and Apply Family
Data Import, Cleaning, and Wrangling in R
Exploratory Data Analysis and Visualization with ggplot2
Core Statistics and Basic Modeling in R
Reproducible Reporting and Data Science Workflows
Capstone: End-to-End R Data Science Project
prerequisites: You need a laptop with permission to install software and packages, plus stable internet access for downloading R and RStudio. Before the course, install the latest versions of R and RStudio and verify you can open RStudio projects and run simple commands. Bringing example datasets or reports from your own work will help you tailor exercises to your context. No coding background is required, but basic familiarity with spreadsheets, CSV files, and descriptive statistics is highly recommended.
topics: Data science & machine learning in practice
